- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.5) within 3–5 days, model often underreacts; adjust downward by 3–8% to align with sentiment shift.
- Model frequently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 2–5% downward bias for days 1–7.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model tends to misalign with mean reversion; apply a 3–7% downward correction toward 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) over 5+ days, model often fails to account for volatility; reduce forecast by 2–5% for days 10–15 to reflect diminishing momentum.
